name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.162.0 — Escape rows learn softMatch: a defect the reviewer saw and filed as advisory is now distinguishable from one review never saw, derived from the correlated review artifact's non-hard survivors, validated by the escape-row writer alongside killedMatch, and counted by the fleet reader as escapes.softMatchTrue. review-legs.js gains --replay, which skips the promise-sweep leg only — its sole input is the spec text, which replay's overlay deliberately withholds — so a replay against a spec amended at review reaches a measurement instead of recording setup-failed. 7.161.0 — The wireframe register becomes shadcn Neutral's own register: wire-tokens.css declares shadcn's eighteen colour-role names and oklch() values verbatim, plus --radius and three pipeline-local roles, replacing eleven plugin-local names under which --muted meant the opposite of shadcn's own sense. wire.css's fifty-two var() references re-base onto the new names, every border-radius moves onto shadcn's four-step scale, and five primitives (button, badge, card, tabs, sheet) are re-drawn to match the registry source, including a sheet shadow that was passing an opaque surface role as a shadow colour. mocks-driver.js gains --refresh-register, which classifies a host's tokens.css by the role names it declares and migrates a retired-register host onto the current one in one command, renaming every var() reference across design/ via the new spec/scripts/lib/wire-roles.js role map. ADR-0013 is narrowed by backlink (ADR-0017): its eleven-role description of the register becomes eighteen roles under shadcn's own names. 7.160.0 — The design atlas answers to a design source: design/chrome-mocks/atlas.html records the approved look of the atlas index, and the doctrine sentence that calls plugin chrome a designed surface now names both chrome mocks as the artifacts a spec editing either must cite as design_source. The atlas's one-frame-per-screen rule, its journey-owned preview links and its ?clean state-switcher suppression are pinned by tests for the first time, and ADR-0016 records the amendment to the superseded frame-per-state promise.
